turns.text: Is it weird that I love true crime podcasts? My sister thinks it's creepy.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not weird at all, millions of people love them. They're often about puzzles, justice and understanding people.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's how I feel. It's the mystery.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. Some people also find them a way to process fears in a safe setting.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: But do you think it's disrespectful to the victims?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It can be, depending on the show. The better ones focus on the victims' stories and treat families with care.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, some of mine are pretty jokey.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Maybe check if their tone sits well with you. There are good serious shows out there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fair. I'll be pickier.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a thoughtful way to enjoy it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My phone storage is full and it says podcasts are taking up twelve gigabytes.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ah, that's probably automatic downloads. Your app may be saving every new episode of every show.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I follow like forty shows.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That'll do it. In the app settings, look for automatic downloads and turn them off, or limit them to the latest episode.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I delete the old ones?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, there's usually an option to remove played episodes. You can also set it to do that automatically.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, found it. / Wait, does it delete my unplayed ones too?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Only if you choose that. Pick remove played episodes only.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Done. That's much better.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Nice. Your phone will thank you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm interviewing my first guest on my podcast tomorrow. How do I ask good questions?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask open questions, ones that can't be answered with yes or no. Start with how or what, or tell me about.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Like, tell me about the first time you baked?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. Then listen and follow up on what they say, rather than rushing to your next question.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm scared of awkward silences.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Silences are often when guests say the best things. Count to three in your head before jumping in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I send them the questions beforehand?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Send the topics, not the exact questions. That keeps answers natural.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good tip. Thanks.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Have fun with it. Enjoy the conversation, that's what listeners will hear.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My nine-year-old wants to listen to podcasts. What's good for kids?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lots of options. Story podcasts with fairy tales, science shows that answer kids' questions, or funny quiz shows.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She loves animals.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then look for a nature show for kids, where a host explores one animal per episode. Usually fifteen minutes or so.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Are they safe? / Like, no weird ads?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most kids' shows keep ads child-friendly, but check a couple of episodes first.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should she listen alone?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: At first, listen together. Then she can pick her own, and you'll know the shows.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Great. She'll love this.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Animal facts at dinner, here you come.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I get more people to listen to my podcast?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A few things work well. Be a guest on similar podcasts, that puts you in front of listeners who already like your kind of show.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, what else?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Share short clips on social media, the funniest or most surprising moments. Clips grab attention better than links.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I hate social media though.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then focus on guesting and asking listeners to tell a friend. Word of mouth is powerful.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Does posting regularly matter?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A lot. Pick a schedule you can keep, even every two weeks, and stick to it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. That's doable.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Consistency beats everything. Keep going.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I just listened to an episode about octopuses and my mind is blown.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Octopuses are amazing. What part blew your mind?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They have three hearts! And blue blood!

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: True. And most of their neurons are in their arms, so each arm can sort of think for itself.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wait, the arms think? / That's terrifying.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A little. They can also change colour and texture in a split second, even though they're colourblind.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do they do that if they can't see colour?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Scientists are still working it out. One idea is their skin can sense light.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm going to need a whole series on octopuses now.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fair. There's plenty to learn.

option_sets.lead_in: I've got a twelve-hour flight coming up and I need help choosing what to listen to.
options: The first one is a true crime series with ten episodes about a bank robbery in the seventies.
Then there's a comedy podcast where three friends rank random things, like cereals or holidays.
There's also a long history show about the Roman Empire, something like twenty hours.
And the last option is a self-improvement podcast about building better habits.
moshi_comment: The Roman history show could easily fill the whole flight, and it's absorbing enough to make the time pass. The comedy one is better if you want to drift in and out. Are you hoping to sleep on the plane?
I'd take the true crime series. Ten episodes is a great binge for a long flight, and the story will pull you along. Save the habits podcast for when you can actually take notes.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm buying gear for my podcast and I can't decide what to get.
options: Option one is a USB microphone for about a hundred dollars that plugs right into my laptop.
Option two is a proper mixer and two XLR microphones, which costs around four hundred.
Then there's a portable recorder with built-in mics, good for recording on the go.
moshi_comment: If it's just you at your desk, the USB microphone is plenty and much easier to set up. The mixer setup only makes sense if you'll regularly have a guest in the same room. Will you record alone?
The portable recorder is great if you plan to interview people out in the world. For a studio-style show with a co-host, though, the two XLR microphones will sound noticeably better.

option_sets.lead_in: I need a new show to binge and I've got three recommendations.
options: A comedy podcast where three friends rank random things, like sandwiches and weather.
A deep investigation into a small-town scandal, twelve episodes with interviews and court tapes.
A calm science show where a host explains one strange fact about nature every episode.
moshi_comment: If you want to laugh, the ranking show sounds like great company. The investigation is the most bingeable, and the science show is perfect for winding down at night.
For a proper binge, I'd go with the investigation, twelve episodes with a real story arc. The comedy one is better for dipping in and out, and the science show is a nice palate cleanser.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm launching my own podcast and I can't pick a format.
options: Me alone, talking about a topic each week, which is easy to schedule but might get lonely.
Interviews with a different guest every episode, more variety, but booking people is a lot of work.
Me and my best friend chatting together, which would be fun, though we tend to go off topic.
Or a mix, mostly solo with a guest once a month.
moshi_comment: Chatting with your best friend sounds the most fun, which helps you stick with it. Interviews add variety but cost time, and the mix could be a nice way to start.
Solo is the simplest, but it's hard to keep energy up alone. I'd try the mix, solo episodes to build your voice and a guest now and then to keep things fresh.

option_sets.lead_in: I need somewhere to record my podcast and I've got three options.
options: My walk-in wardrobe, which is free and quiet thanks to all the clothes, but it's hot and cramped.
A rented studio downtown, fifty an hour, with proper soundproofing and an engineer.
The library's free recording booth, but you have to book it a week in advance.
moshi_comment: The wardrobe is a classic for a reason, clothes kill echo. The library booth is a great free upgrade if you can plan ahead, and the studio is worth it for special episodes.
I'd start in the wardrobe and see how it goes. If the heat gets too much, try the library booth, and keep the studio for interviews with important guests.
